component.name: Elements Extract
component.summary: Extract audio, video and subtitle tracks, translate subtitles offline
Extrae pistas de audio, vídeo y subtítulos; traduce subtítulos sin conexión

description.p: Elements Extract is a graphical batch extractor for audio, video and subtitle tracks, with offline neural subtitle translation (bergamot-translator) and embedding of the translation back into the video (remux) without re-encoding. Six tiny models for English, Spanish, French and Portuguese are bundled, so those pairs work offline from the first launch. Your files never leave your machine.

Elements Extract es un extractor gráfico por lotes de pistas de audio, vídeo y subtítulos, con traducción neuronal de subtítulos sin conexión (bergamot-translator) e incrustación de la traducción en el vídeo (remux) sin re-codificar. Se incluyen seis modelos tiny para inglés, español, francés y portugués, por lo que esos pares funcionan sin conexión desde el primer arranque. Tus archivos nunca salen de tu máquina.

description.p: Fixed Windows subtitle translation: release workflows now flatten model archives with --strip-components=1 and bundle all six tiny language pairs. Older nested v1.2.12 installs are also detected, so reinstalling is not required.

The model manager separates bundled models (included, not deletable) from downloaded ones, lists every registry model with a search box and details, and makes any newly installed language available in the source/target selectors.
Redesigned About dialog, updated help and READMEs, new English screenshots, and completed English/Portuguese translations.
Windows build fix: use the Qt 6 redirect API supported by Qt 6.8, stop passing the GCC-only -s flag to MSVC, and remove deprecated API warnings.
Build fix: removed the zlib dependency so the Windows build configures cleanly. The nOCR template database is now shipped uncompressed and loaded directly from resources.
Layout fix: the Cancel and Start Extraction buttons now stay visible in a fixed footer, and the activity log no longer shrinks the work area.
Added an update notifier backed by the GitHub Releases API, with a manual "Check for updates" action in the Help menu and release notes with a download link.
Build fixes: Linux CI now installs zlib1g-dev and the nOCR template database is shipped as a tracked resource, so clean checkouts compile again.
Public documentation and English screenshots updated for AppImageHub, covering the online subtitle backends and the experimental image OCR.

Default online subtitle backend switched to the opensubtitles.org XML-RPC API, with direct download links and anonymous search like VLSub in VLC; the official opensubtitles.com REST API remains available in Settings.

Optional, experimental image subtitle OCR with nOCR: extracts PGS/VobSub frames with ffmpeg and writes a translatable .srt, keeping the original .mks copy if recognition fails. Progress is shown in the log and a full episode can take several minutes.
Online search now combines file hash and title/season/episode results without duplicates, so releases with only English hash matches also find translations in other languages.

Prefer the target language from Settings when searching online subtitles: it is highlighted and its results are sorted first. When no subtitle exists in that language, the app offers downloading another language and translating it with the existing triangular path. Help updated.

Search subtitles manually for the selected video or in batch for several videos from the file list, with editable per-file queries. Credentials are stored in the operating system secure keyring (Secret Service, Credential Manager or Keychain) instead of plaintext settings.
Search, download and translate subtitles from OpenSubtitles.com using your own account. Downloads are unpacked (ZIP/GZIP/RAR) before offline translation, with hash-based matching and title fallback.
Extract image-based subtitles (Blu-ray PGS, DVD/VobSub, DVB, XSUB) verbatim as .mks via stream copy. Subtitle codecs and languages are now shown per file, with clearer ffprobe/ffmpeg error messages.
Translate standalone subtitle files (.srt/.ass/.ssa/.vtt) opened from the desktop context menu, without video extraction. Desktop entry now advertises subtitle MIME types.
English UI under C/POSIX locales, bundled ffprobe on Windows and portable executable lookup.
Subtitle filter by language, translation with embedding (remux), triangular translation, model manager.
